title: James Davolos on the MicroCapClub: A Deep Dive on Exchanges (October 2026)
gist: Teaser page for a 66-minute MicroCapClub video in which Horizon Kinetics' James Davolos argues exchanges have beaten their local markets over 20 years, that derivatives are the industry's strongest moat, and that inflation and volatility can benefit exchanges. The disclosures reveal the firm holds discretion over a substantial share of TPL and MIAX, possibly making it an affiliate restricted from selling, and refer to co-founder Murray Stahl as 'the late'.

insights.claim: James Davolos of Horizon Kinetics argues that exchanges have outperformed the local equity markets they operate in over the past 20 years.
insights.speaker: Horizon Kinetics
insights.so_what: Owning the exchange operator rather than the local index has been, per Horizon Kinetics, a superior way to get country-market exposure.
insights.quote: explain why exchanges have outperformed their local markets over the past 20 years

insights.claim: Horizon Kinetics views derivatives trading as the strongest competitive moat within the exchange industry.
insights.speaker: Horizon Kinetics
insights.so_what: Within exchange stocks, operators with derivatives franchises would be the preferred durable holdings over cash-equity-heavy venues.
insights.quote: why derivatives are the strongest moat in the industry

insights.claim: Inflation and market volatility can benefit exchange operators, positioning exchanges as inflation-beneficiary assets rather than victims of turbulent markets.
insights.speaker: Horizon Kinetics
insights.so_what: Exchanges can act as a hedge in an inflationary, high-volatility regime, consistent with their inclusion in an inflation-beneficiaries strategy.
insights.quote: why inflation and volatility can benefit exchanges

insights.claim: Horizon Kinetics has discretion over a substantial percentage of the outstanding shares of TPL and MIAX, so it may be deemed an affiliate and could be restricted from selling those stocks on behalf of client accounts.
insights.speaker: Horizon Kinetics
insights.so_what: Signals deep, concentrated conviction in TPL and the exchange operator MIAX, and a liquidity overhang or sale constraint that matters to other holders.
insights.quote: because the Firm has discretion over a substantial percentage of the outstanding shares of TPL and MIAX, it may be deemed to be an affiliate of TPL and MIAX
insights.locator: Furthermore, because the Firm has discretion

insights.claim: The Horizon Kinetics Inflation Beneficiaries ETF (INFL) is an actively managed, non-diversified fund that invests in real-asset-linked securities, including foreign, emerging-market and small- and mid-cap holdings, and can concentrate in few names.
insights.speaker: Horizon Kinetics
insights.so_what: INFL is the listed vehicle for the firm's inflation-beneficiary thesis, exchanges included, and it carries concentration and single-stock risk.
insights.quote: The Fund is non‐diversified, meaning it may concentrate its assets in fewer individual holdings than a diversified fund.

insights.claim: Horizon Kinetics co-founder Murray Stahl is referred to as 'the late' Murray Stahl, indicating he has died, and James Davolos offers reflections on him.
insights.speaker: Horizon Kinetics
insights.so_what: A key-person transition at a firm with concentrated, idiosyncratic positions; watch for continuity in strategy and stewardship of the TPL and MIAX stakes.
insights.quote: The conversation wraps up with James’ reflections on the late Murray Stahl, Co-Founder of Horizon Kinetics.
